sections.heading: Future tense or ir a?
sections.body:
In everyday Latin American speech, *ir a* + infinitive is the usual way to talk about plans: *Voy a viajar en julio.* The simple future is used for predictions, promises, more distant or less certain things, and in writing: *Mañana lloverá en el norte.* (weather forecast) *Te llamaré, te lo prometo.* *Algún día viviré en la playa.*

(You'll see in B1 that the future also expresses guesses about the present: *¿Dónde estará Juan?* — I wonder where Juan is.)

examples: Tomorrow it will rain in the north.
Algún día viviré en la playa.
Someday I'll live at the beach.
What will you do next year?
We'll have a meeting on Monday.
No podré ir a la fiesta.
I won't be able to go to the party.
There will be lots of people.
El pronóstico dice que hará sol.
The forecast says it will be sunny.
Las temperaturas bajarán en el sur.
Temperatures will drop in the south.
Dentro de diez años, hablaré español perfectamente.
In ten years, I'll speak Spanish perfectly.
Will you know how to get there?
El tren llegará a las cinco.
The train will arrive at five.
My kids will want to come.
En el futuro, trabajaremos desde casa.
In the future, we'll work from home.
They'll travel to Chile in December.
